subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Lapsang Souchong: Smoked Tea
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Lapsang Souchong: Smoked Tea.

hook.text: Lapsang Souchong is tea dried over burning pinewood. It smells like a campfire in a cup.

buildup.text: Legend says soldiers camped in a tea factory, delaying production. Workers rushed drying over pine fires.

discovery.text: The smoke from Masson pine infuses the leaves with compounds called guaiacol and syringol—the flavor of smoke.

twist.text: Winston Churchill was reportedly a Lapsang fan. Some say it reminds drinkers of whisky without the alcohol.

climax.text: Original Lapsang Souchong from Wuyi Mountains is rare. Most commercial versions use artificial smoke flavor.

punchline.text: Pine smoke, bold leaves, a flavor that divides every room.
